newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary agency decides asset swap with Postabank.
newsitem.headline: Hungary agency decides asset swap with Postabank.

text.p: Hungary's state privatisation agency APV said that it decided on Thursday on an asset swap worth 10.73 billion forints with Postabank Rt, a bank hit by a wave of withdrawals earlier this year.
"According to the government's decision, the value of the assets to be swapped will be equal at 10.73 billion forints," APV Chairman Arpad Kovacs told a news conference.
Postabank will receive minority stakes in 24 firms, including five regional gas and electricity distributors, and will give real estate in exchange.
The move will improve the liquidity of the assets of the bank, from which depositors withdrew some 24 billion forints five months ago after rumours about the bank's possible insolvency.

The government is the most influential shareholder in Postabank through stakes held indirectly, but the bank and its advisor, SBC Warburg, are seeking strategic investors to raise Postabank's capital later this year.
An APV official told Reuters that Postabank was likely to sell most of the stakes it would get in the asset swap in a relatively short time.

The foreign investors which acquired large minority stakes in the regional gas distributors, at the end of 1995, including Bayernwerk, Italgas and Gaz de France have a pre-emption right for buying the stakes which Postabank gets, the official said.
The gas distributor stakes to be received by Postabank range from 0.58 percent to 8.93 percent, while the electricity distributor stakes are between 4.39 percent and 8.66 percent.

Postabank will also receive 3.67 percent of the salami maker Herz Szalamigyar Rt, a member of the Pick group, and 3.74 percent of drugs maker Alkaloida, which is majority owned by ICN Pharmaceuticals.
Originally the government decided on a 17 billion forint worth asset swap but APV did not accept company stakes and some of the real estates offered by Postbank, Kovacs said.
